svg.text: Fault chain: likely cause, then mechanism, then fault.

text.tspan: Pointed to by: your lead hip had turned
31° at impact, where about 45° is

7% of body height, address to impact. Key
frames: address and impact.

svg.text: Fault. Decided by the rule table: 7% is past the 4% threshold.

text.tspan: Your hips moved toward the ball on the way down: by 7% of your
body height between address and impact, well past the 4% where
we call it early extension. When the hips push forward, your
arms lose their room, so you stand up out of the shot to make
space. That is why it can feel like you stay down while the club
arrives from a different spot each time. The likely reason is
restricted hip rotation: your lead hip had turned 31° at impact,
where about 45° is typical. We cannot measure that directly, so
treat it as likely, not certain. Work on turning, not on holding
still: the wall drill teaches your hips to turn back instead of
forward, and the 90/90 stretch gives them room to do it.

svg.text: Possible, not a verified fault. No drill for it yet.

text.tspan: Capped at medium: from down the line it can only be measured from the hand
path.

svg.text: One drill for the fault, one mobility exercise for its likely cause. Print them, or keep this page open in your bag.

g.text: Trail glute stays on the wall

text.tspan: Set up with your backside touching
a wall, or a golf bag.
Keep your trail glute on the wall
through impact.
rotation

rotation
rotation
Sit with both knees bent to 90°,
one leg in front, one to the side.
Rotate both knees to the other
side, chest tall.
Generic guidance, not medical advice — see
a physiotherapist if you feel pain.

svg.text: Answers are based only on this analysis. The coach will not add faults, numbers or drills.
Why does it feel like I’m staying down when I’m not?

text.tspan: Staying down is usually felt through your head and eyes, so a move lower in the body
is easy to miss. Yours is lower: between address and impact your hips moved toward
the ball by 7% of your body height. In the impact frame your backside sits past the
pink dashed line where it started. In the wall drill, notice the moment your trail
glute leaves the wall. That is the move you cannot feel yet.
